identity: Neutral nitrous oxide N-N-O, CAS 10024-97-2, linear singlet ground state; not cyclic N2O, an N-O-N connectivity, or N2O+.
recommendation: Evaluate a NASA-thermal/ATcT candidate against a retained-thermal energy-only control in a separate follow-up. Modern partition data favor investigating the high-temperature JANAF thermal deficit, but the present source review does not adopt either candidate.
science: JANAF and NASA have a small balanced energy difference but the energy-aligned JANAF/NASA ratio falls to 0.912 at 4000 K. The current literal fit follows JANAF to about one percent at the sampled nodes. ATcT lowers JANAF atomization energy by 0.829 kJ/mol; its thermal-preserving effect is distinct from the temperature-dependent thermal discrepancy.
modern: The 2025 TIPS assessment was read with its N2O direct-sum/product-approximation discussion. For the principal 14N2-16O isotopologue the direct-sum/product crossover is 4520 K, above the reviewed upper limit; other isotopologues have different limits. Exact pinned principal-isotope TIPS nodes, divided by nuclear-spin product 9 once, give Q/NASA about 1.00023 at 1500 K and 0.97053 at 4000 K. They therefore do not reproduce either older source exactly. Sparse Q nodes here are not differentiated into calorics. The 2025 ABG-IMRHT/Ames-2000K paper supplies an additional modern line-list lead; its abstract was inspected and the full numerical model was not retrieved.
importance: N2O has atmospheric radiative and chemical relevance beyond this hot hydrogen-rich grid. Its tiny equilibrium abundance here cannot evaluate cooler, biological, oxidizing or photochemical production.
conventions: 14N2-16O has nuclear-spin product 9; its two N atoms occupy inequivalent positions, so a homonuclear-rotor symmetry division must not be added. The source tables already include molecular degeneracies. TIPS is a principal-isotope internal-state proxy combined with the same natural-mass translation as NASA; no isotope-mixture entropy is added.
followup: Build continuous NASA/ATcT and retained-thermal energy-only candidates, validate all caloric derivatives and perform current-network substitutions. A TIPS-based replacement would additionally need a smooth state/caloric representation and treatment of its source crossover, not extrapolation of sparse partition nodes. No unavailable ancestral book is required for the bounded candidate calculation or source-review merge.
